title: Integral split roots force splitting at every normalization residue field
statement:
Let $S$ be an integral scheme with function field $K$, let $M/K$ be a finite extension, and let $a:W\to S$ be the normalization of $S$ in $M$ [def-fin-normalization-extension]. Let $s\in S$, put $R=\mathcal O_{S,s}$ and $F=\kappa(s)$, and let $E=\operatorname{Spec}D$ be a finite etale $F$-scheme. Suppose given a finite set $B$, finite separable extensions $F_b/F$, an $F$-algebra isomorphism $D\cong\prod_{b\in B}F_b$, a finite Galois extension $L/F$ with $F$-embeddings $F_b\hookrightarrow L$, and a primitive element $\alpha$ with $L=F(\alpha)$. Let $q\in F[T]$ be its monic minimal polynomial of degree $d\ge1$, and let $f\in R[T]$ be a monic lift of $q$ of degree $d$. Assume a full factorization $f(T)=\prod_{\nu=1}^d(T-\beta_\nu)$ with $\beta_\nu\in M$. Then every $\beta_\nu$ belongs to the integral closure $\overline R^{\,M}$. For every point $w\in W$ with $a(w)=s$, the canonical map $\overline R^{\,M}\to\mathcal O_{W,w}\to\kappa(w)$ gives
$$q(T)=\prod_{\nu=1}^d(T-\overline\beta_\nu)\quad\text{in }\kappa(w)[T].$$
For each such $w$ there is an $F$-embedding $L\hookrightarrow\kappa(w)$. For every $b\in B$ one has an isomorphism of $\kappa(w)$-algebras
$$F_b\otimes_F\kappa(w)\cong\prod_{1\le j\le [F_b:F]}\kappa(w).$$
Consequently $D\otimes_F\kappa(w)\cong\prod_{1\le j\le n}\kappa(w)$ for $n=\sum_{b\in B}[F_b:F]$, and $E\times_F\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)$ is isomorphic over $\kappa(w)$ to the disjoint union of $n$ copies of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)$. Empty $B$ and $E$ are allowed. No normality, projectivity or Noetherian hypothesis on $S$, no group action, and no Galois hypothesis on $M/K$ are required.

Integral scheme, function field, residue field, finite morphism, etaleness, fibre product, polynomial ring, field extension and separability use [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-sc-function-field], [def-weil-residue-field], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-weil-polynomial-ring], [def-pc-field-extension] and [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Finite Galois means finite-dimensional, separable and normal (every minimal polynomial splits).

proof.text: Fix any $w$ above $s$. Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $s$, and write $\mathfrak p$ for its prime. By [def-fin-normalization-extension], $a^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}C_A$, where $C_A$ is the integral closure of $A$ in $M$; write $\mathfrak Q\subset C_A$ for $w$, so $\mathfrak Q\cap A=\mathfrak p$. The stalk identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization] give $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathcal O_{W,w}=(C_A)_{\mathfrak Q}$, compatibly with the structural map. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], $C=(A\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}C_A$ inside $M$: localizing $M$ at these nonzero elements leaves $M$ unchanged. Since all elements of $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ avoid $\mathfrak Q$, the fraction map $c/t\mapsto c/t$ defines the required canonical map $C\to(C_A)_{\mathfrak Q}=\mathcal O_{W,w}$. Its composite with the residue quotient has restriction to $R$ equal to $R\to F\to H$, where $H=\kappa(w)$, by [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tag 0307, lemma-integral-closure-localize; Schemes 01HV and the affine stalk maps; agent assembly

proof.text: The inclusion $C\subset M$ is injective. Thus the given polynomial identity, whose coefficients and roots lie in $C$, is already an equality in $C[T]$ (compare each coefficient). Apply $C\to H$ coefficientwise. The image of $f$ is the image of $q$, since $f$ lifts $q$ and the composite on $R$ is $R\to F\to H$. Ring homomorphisms preserve finite products, $T$, and constants, giving $q_H(T)=\prod_{\nu=1}^d(T-\overline\beta_\nu)$ in $H[T]$. This proves the displayed reduction identity for the arbitrary $w$ chosen in step 2.

Because $d\ge1$, put $z=\overline\beta_1\in H$; step 3 gives $q_H(z)=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-polynomial-quotient-field-iso], evaluation at $\alpha$ identifies $F[T]/(q)$ with $F(\alpha)=L$. Evaluation $g\mapsto g_H(z)$ kills every multiple of $q$, so $[g]\mapsto g_H(z)$ is a well-defined unital $F$-algebra map from this quotient to $H$: representatives differing by $q h$ have evaluations differing by $q_H(z)h_H(z)=0$. Composing with the inverse isomorphism gives $\iota:L\to H$. It is injective: if a nonzero $x$ mapped to zero, $1=xx^{-1}$ would map to zero in the field $H$. This proves the required $F$-embedding.

source.place: Simple algebraic extension presentation used in Tag 030N, lemma-primitive-element; agent evaluation argument

proof.text: Fix $b\in B$. Apply [lem-zl-finite-separable-tensor-primitive-presentation] with $k=F$, $E=F_b$, $K=H$. It supplies $\gamma_b$, its monic irreducible minimal polynomial $P_b$, $F_b=F(\gamma_b)$, and an $H$-algebra isomorphism $H\otimes_F F_b\cong H[T]/((P_b)_H)$. If $r_b=[F_b:F]$, then $\deg P_b=r_b$: by [lem-weil-pbc-simple-algebraic-extension-power-basis], $1,\gamma_b,\ldots,\gamma_b^{r_b-1}$ is a basis. A relation of degree less than $r_b$ contradicts independence; spanning expresses $\gamma_b^{r_b}$ as a linear combination of those powers, giving a monic annihilating polynomial of degree $r_b$. Minimality of $P_b$ proves both inequalities. In particular $r_b\ge1$.

source.place: Tag 037P, lemma-field-extension-geometrically-irreducible, primitive-element tensor presentation; Fields Tag 030N

proof.text: Let $j_b:F_b\hookrightarrow L$ be the supplied embedding. The minimal polynomial of $j_b(\gamma_b)$ over $F$ is $P_b$, because evaluation has the same kernel after the injective map $j_b$. Normality of $L/F$, in exactly the sense stated in the item, gives a full factorization of $P_b$ into $r_b$ monic linear factors over $L$. These roots are pairwise distinct. Indeed, separability of $F_b/F$ gives $UP_b+VP_b^{\prime}=1$ by [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and [def-pc-separable-polynomial]. A repeated root $c$ in the linear factorization would give $P_b(c)=P_b^{\prime}(c)=0$ (differentiate the product), contradicting this identity at $c$. Applying the injective $\iota:L\hookrightarrow H$ gives a factorization $(P_b)_H=\prod_{j=1}^{r_b}(T-c_{b,j})$ with pairwise distinct $c_{b,j}\in H$.

source.place: Tag 09HM, definition-normal; separability and the elementary derivative test for a repeated linear factor

proof.text: By [lem-pc-polynomial-quotient-distinct-linear-crt], evaluation at the distinct $c_{b,j}$ identifies $H[T]/((P_b)_H)$ with $\prod_{j=1}^{r_b}H$ as $H$-algebras. Compose with step 5. To put the tensor factors in the order required by the statement, use $F_b\otimes_F H\to H\otimes_F F_b$, $x\otimes h\mapsto h\otimes x$. The bilinearity relations in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] make this linear map well-defined, and the same formula in reverse is its inverse. It preserves $1$ and multiplication, since $(x\otimes h)(y\otimes k)=xy\otimes hk$ by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]; it also preserves the $H$-structure maps. Hence $F_b\otimes_F H\cong\prod_{j=1}^{r_b}H$ as $H$-algebras.

source.place: Tag 00U3, lemma-etale-over-field, separable polynomial case; explicit tensor symmetry and CRT assembly

proof.text: Tensor the supplied $F$-algebra isomorphism $D\cong\prod_{b\in B}F_b$ with $H$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product] the coordinate map $(\prod_b F_b)\otimes_F H\to\prod_b(F_b\otimes_F H)$, $(x_b)_b\otimes h\mapsto(x_b\otimes h)_b$, is an isomorphism of $F$-modules. It is an $H$-algebra isomorphism as well: the pure-tensor product formula of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] shows preservation of products and $1$, and it sends $1\otimes h$ to $(1\otimes h)_b$. Pure tensors span by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], so bilinearity extends these equalities to all tensors. Compose with step 7 for each $b$ and reindex the coordinates $(b,j)$ to obtain $D\otimes_F H\cong\prod_{j=1}^n H$, $n=\sum_b r_b$. For $B=\varnothing$ both products and the tensor with $D=0$ are the zero ring, so the same assertion includes the empty case.

source.place: Agent algebra-compatibility calculation for finite-product tensor comparison in the residue splitting argument

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $E\times_F\operatorname{Spec}H\cong\operatorname{Spec}(D\otimes_F H)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}H$. Apply $\operatorname{Spec}$ to the $H$-algebra isomorphism in step 8. Finally specialize [lem-sbc-finite-product-principal-open] to the coefficient ring $H$, the element $1$, and the $n$ constant component algebras $H$. Its principal opens $D(1)$ are the whole spectra, so it gives $\coprod_{j=1}^n\operatorname{Spec}H\cong\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_{j=1}^nH)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}H$. Composition (inverting this last isomorphism) gives precisely the asserted disjoint union over $H$. The cited result permits $n=0$; the resulting scheme is empty. Every construction was for arbitrary $w$ over $s$, so all conclusions hold at every such point.
